issues.title: Inconsistent ID prefix for document-typed nodes
issues.detail: 14 nodes have type=document, but the ID-prefix convention is split: 6 use 'document:' (CLAUDE.md, CMakeLists.txt, README.md, move-src.txt, s7_3/README.md, s7_5/README.md) while 8 use 'file:' (Linux/RK3568/*.md, LICENSE.txt files, etc.). The merge script only normalized func:/function:/func-type prefixes and left document nodes alone, so file-path-based documents kept 'file:' while the LLM-batched ones got 'document:'. The graph is internally consistent (all 13 edges referencing the file:-prefixed documents point at those exact IDs, zero dangling), so connectivity is fine. But a downstream consumer keyed on ID prefix rather than the 'type' field would mis-bucket half the documents.
issues.recommendation: Optional: standardize document nodes to a single prefix (either all 'document:' or all 'file:') and rewrite the affected edges accordingly. Low priority since 'type' is the reliable discriminator.

notes: Node ID integrity is solid: 0 dangling edges in the assembled graph (the 8 drops from the merge report were already removed; no additional subtle ones found).
Function/class node IDs are consistently '<type>:<filePath>[:<name>]' and every function's filePath resolves to a present file node (0 orphan functions).
All 23 non-empty importMap entries from scan-result.json are present as 'imports' edges in the graph (0 missing cross-batch import edges).
Layer coverage is complete: all 62 APP/ code files and all 20 Core/ code files from the inventory are present as file nodes. No missing custom APP/ source files.
No genuine duplicate file nodes (the 114 filePath collisions are expected file-vs-its-own-functions/classes sharing filePath; 0 files appear as two separate file-type nodes).

File-category / layer tagging is reasonable: 21 nodes tagged 'app-layer', 15 'no-rtos-dependency', HAL/driver/vendor/cubemx/boilerplate tags are applied to the CubeMX/HAL/Middleware boilerplate, and rk3568-tagged nodes cover the companion-computer source. CubeMX-generated files (main.c, freertos.c, gpio.c, spi.c, usart.c, dma.c, stm32f7xx_*.c) are correctly tagged 'cubemx'.
Complexity values are clean (simple 269 / moderate 207 / complex 98); no unknown values survived. No empty/missing summaries.

Coverage gap (source-side, not a graph error): 6 Tools/*.mjs verification scripts (verify_power_monitor, verify_rate_pid_mixer, verify_rc_failsafe, verify_rc_setpoint, verify_s7_8_e2e, verify_s7_8_trace) are in the scan inventory but absent from the assembled graph. They were never present in any batch file (0 mentions across all 20 batches), so the merge could not produce them. They are repo tooling, not firmware source — low impact, but a re-scan would surface them. GETFUN_F722_FreeRTOS.ioc IS present (config node).

The dropped-edge examples in the merge report are explained by ID mismatches, not by missing files: e.g. CMakeLists.txt, s7_6_serial.cpp/.hpp, APP/Src/bsp/usb_cdc_transport.c all exist as nodes. The failures were source-name mismatches (e.g. 'CDC_TransmitCplt_FS' vs the actual 'usb_cdc_transport_transmit_complete_from_isr' function id), i.e. the LLM emitted edges to nodes that were never created. No recovery action needed.
summary: The assembled graph (574 nodes, 475 edges) is internally consistent and semantically sound. No dangling edges, no orphan functions, all importMap cross-batch edges intact, and the custom APP/ + Core/ firmware layers are fully covered. The one concrete inconsistency is cosmetic: document-typed nodes use a mixed ID-prefix scheme (6 'document:' vs 8 'file:'), which is safe because edges match the exact IDs and the 'type' field is the reliable discriminator. The only real coverage gap is the 6 Tools/*.mjs scripts, which were never analyzed by any batch and thus cannot be recovered by the merge. No graph edits were required; the graph is dashboard-ready.
